territorial_scope.description: Applies to employers and workers covered by the California Labor Code, including state and local government employers.

evidence.quote: “Worker” means any natural person who is an employee of, or an independent contractor providing service to, or through, a business or a state or local governmental entity in any workplace.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Adds Labor Code Part 5.5.5 on employers' use of automated decision systems (ADS): written pre-use and post-use notices to workers, bar on relying solely on ADS for discipline, termination or deactivation, worker data access, and Labor Commissioner and prosecutor enforcement.
summary.long: Adds Labor Code Part 5.5.5 (§§1520–1539) on automated decision systems (ADS) used in employment. Employers must give written notice to affected workers at least 30 days before first deploying an ADS for employment-related decisions other than hiring (existing users by April 1, 2026; new workers within 30 days of hiring), notify job applicants of hiring-related ADS use, and maintain a list of ADS in use. Employers may not use ADS to violate labor or civil rights laws, infer protected status, take adverse action for exercising legal rights, or collect worker data for undisclosed purposes. Discipline, termination or deactivation may not rest solely on ADS; where ADS output is primarily relied on, a human reviewer must review it and a post-decision notice is required. Customer ratings may not be the only or primary ADS input. Workers may request a copy of their own data from the most recent 12 months primarily used by an ADS in such decisions, once every 12 months. The Labor Commissioner and public prosecutors enforce the part; violators face a $500 civil penalty. Carve-outs: collective bargaining agreements that explicitly waive the part; federal contract compliance; CCPA rules.

relations.note: Section 1537 provides that an employer subject to the CCPA is subject to privacy-related automated decisionmaking technology regulations adopted by the California Privacy Protection Agency under Civil Code Sections 1798.185 and 1798.199.40; Section 1536 makes this exception to its notice-compliance provision.

notes: The document is bill text with no version, date or legislative history; the 'failed' status and 'dead' stage come from registry metadata only. Internal points: Section 1522(a) limits the pre-use notice to decisions other than hiring, while Section 1522(d) requires notice to job applicants where an ADS is used for hiring decisions. Section 1522(a)(2) refers to the date 'this title takes effect', but the text is a Labor Code Part and contains no effective-date provision. Section 1534 states that the part does not preempt more protective local ordinances; this is a non-preemption clause and is not coded as a preemption relation. Section 1536 refers to 'any other state law' without naming any instrument, so no relation is coded for it. The section_status entry below is required by the schema and is not a finding; relations are listed above.
